title: Business Requirements Document — Requirements Chat 2

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Management System (HMS) is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing comprehensive hospital operations. The strategic rationale for this system is to streamline and digitize critical workflows including patient information management, medical records, appointments, and operational departments such as billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. By implementing a unified system with role-based access control, the hospital aims to enhance operational efficiency, improve patient care through accessible electronic medical records (EMR), and ensure strict compliance with healthcare data privacy standards. The system will support a complete lifecycle of patient care, from registration and consultation to treatment, laboratory/pharmacy interactions, billing, and follow-up, as well as inpatient management from admission to discharge.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
**Business Objectives:**
1. Centralize hospital operations to eliminate data silos across departments (Reception, Doctors, Nursing, Lab, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory).
2. Implement robust role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure data security and privacy for sensitive medical information.
3. Digitize the complete patient journey, including OPD/IPD workflows, to reduce administrative overhead and improve patient experience.
4. Provide real-time visibility into hospital resources, including bed/ward availability, medicine inventory, and staff schedules.

**Success Metrics:**
- **Operational Efficiency:** Reduction in manual processing time for patient registration, appointment scheduling, and billing.
- **Data Integrity:** 100% accuracy in electronic medical records, diagnosis, and prescription tracking.
- **System Availability:** High availability of the platform to support continuous hospital operations.
- **Compliance:** Zero unauthorized access incidents to Protected Health Information (PHI), adhering to HIPAA and GDPR standards.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In Scope:**
- **Patient Management:** Registration, profile management, OPD/IPD management, admission/discharge/transfer, and patient portal for viewing appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills.
- **Clinical Operations:** Appointment scheduling, queue management, doctor availability, electronic medical records (EMR), diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
- **Support Departments:** Laboratory test requests/reports, pharmacy prescriptions/medicine inventory, bed/ward management, and inventory/procurement.
- **Financial Operations:** Billing, payments, insurance management, invoices, receipts, and hospital expenses.
- **Administrative Functions:** Staff management, dashboards for various roles, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit logs, data validation, backup/recovery, and security.

**Out of Scope:**
- Hardware procurement and physical infrastructure setup (cloud or on-premise deployment is a technical constraint, not a business deliverable).
- Integration with external third-party systems not explicitly mentioned (e.g., external insurance providers, though insurance management is in scope).
- Mobile application development (source specifies responsive web UI).

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
The system will support the following role-based access personas, each with specific governance and operational responsibilities:

- **Admin:** System configuration, user management, and overall oversight.
- **Doctor:** Clinical decision-making, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
- **Nurse:** Patient care, nursing notes, vital signs monitoring, and treatment administration.
- **Receptionist:** Patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
- **Pharmacist:** Prescription processing, medicine inventory management, and dispensing.
- **Lab Technician:** Laboratory test requests, sample processing, and report generation.
- **Accountant:** Billing, payments, insurance claims, invoices, and financial reporting.
- **Patient:** Access to personal medical history, appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills via the patient portal.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: System must allow registration of patients and management of their profiles, including allergies and medical history.
Patient can be registered with all required fields; profile is accessible to authorized roles.
System must support scheduling appointments, managing queues, and tracking doctor availability.
Appointments can be scheduled, rescheduled, and cancelled; queue status is updated in real-time.
System must manage Outpatient (OPD) and Inpatient (IPD) workflows, including admission, discharge, and transfer.
Patients can be admitted, transferred, and discharged with proper documentation and bed allocation.
System must maintain comprehensive EMR including diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, and nursing notes.
All clinical data is recorded, searchable, and accessible to authorized roles with audit trails.
System must handle laboratory test requests, sample tracking, and report generation.
Lab tests can be requested, processed, and reports are linked to the patient's EMR.
System must manage pharmacy prescriptions, medicine inventory, and procurement.
Prescriptions are processed, inventory levels are updated, and low-stock alerts are generated.
System must support billing, payments, insurance management, and generation of invoices/receipts.
Bills are generated accurately, payments are recorded, and insurance claims are processed.
Patients must be able to view appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history via a secure portal.
Patients can log in and view their personal data; access is restricted to their own records.
System must enforce role-based access for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
Users can only access modules and data relevant to their role; unauthorized access is blocked.
System must maintain immutable audit logs for all actions and ensure secure authentication and data encryption.
All user actions are logged; PHI is encrypted at rest and in transit; audit logs are tamper-proof.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
**Assumptions:**
1. The hospital will provide accurate and complete data for patient registration and staff onboarding.
2. Users will have basic digital literacy to interact with the web-based interface.
3. The system will be deployed in a secure environment (cloud or on-premise) with appropriate network security measures.

**Operational Constraints:**
1. **Compliance:** The system must comply with HIPAA and GDPR (if EU patients are involved) for data privacy and security.
2. **Data Standards:** Medical data should adhere to HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards where applicable.
3. **Performance:** The system must support high availability and fast API responses to handle concurrent users during peak hours.
4. **Security:** PHI must be encrypted at rest using AES-256, and audit trails must be immutable.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
**Compliance Baseline:**
- **HIPAA:** Ensure all Protected Health Information (PHI) is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (HTTPS). Implement strict access controls and maintain immutable audit trails to meet §164.312 requirements.
- **GDPR:** If EU patients are involved, ensure data minimization, right to erasure, and consent management are implemented.
- **HL7 FHIR/DICOM:** Ensure interoperability with other healthcare systems by adhering to standard data formats.

**Risk Baseline:**
- **Data Breach:** High risk due to sensitive medical data. Mitigated by RBAC, encryption, and regular security audits.
- **System Downtime:** High risk due to critical nature of hospital operations. Mitigated by high availability architecture, regular backups (RTO < 1h, RPO < 5min), and disaster recovery plans.
- **User Error:** Medium risk due to complex workflows. Mitigated by intuitive UI, data validation, and training programs.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
